response_consumed_stops.reason: unknown positive trap coordinates outside the frozen response-blind registry

primary_conclusion.supported: The prospectively frozen response-blind whole-network structural rule did not successfully forecast later falsifiable-world survival regimes in the fixed NEON programme and systematically underpredicted world survival among scored sites.
primary_conclusion.failed_hypothesis: Response-blind whole-network structural adequacy plus the one-step horizon-realization ratio is sufficient to anticipate whether a finite world universe will falsify, contract, or saturate after positive evidence.
primary_conclusion.endpoint_regime_anomaly_resolution: The finite-world framework is not intrinsically restricted to endpoint outcomes: two independently scored sites produced genuine intermediate contraction. However, saturation dominated seven of nine scored sites.

not_supported: claiming all finite-world systems are inherently saturated
assigning a biological regime to any of the seven registry-mismatch sites
generalizing this guild-level NEON endpoint to taxon-level systems without a new protocol
using the result to alter the closed EOG-WF Layer-B predictive conclusion
next_theoretical_question: Whether survival regime is identifiable from response-blind global graph structure at all when compatibility depends on the unknown placement of positive nodes.
